messages:
elaine: Drafting the benchmark narrative — want to push a slightly different framing: 'tokens-per-dollar curve' as the headline, not just latency vs cost. Makes the economics feel more actionable.

mike: Interesting. How do you visualize that for non-technical buyers?

elaine: Idea: a single curve chart showing tokens/USD on Y and latency buckets as small inset sparkline per point. So you can see both economics and latency at a glance.

ryan: Love the mini-sparklines. Also propose a second hero: a step chart that shows cost tiers (hosted / dedicated / private) for a sample workload, with annotated break-even points.

zoe: For landing flow, clicks on the curve -> micro-form (infra preference + tokens/day + use case). Micro-form answers map to routing: >200M tokens/day -> SDR; infra=private -> AE outreach; others -> nurture.

mike: Social hooks to test: 1) "How many tokens per dollar is your app getting?" 2) "See the tokens-per-dollar curve for real workloads."

elaine: Messaging guardrails: avoid absolute proprietary numbers on public hero. Use ranges and label methodology slide with exact model names and quantization.

product-bot: benchmark-export ready at /eng-ml/benchmarks/179999/export.csv

ryan: Design asks: colorblind palette, compact legend, hover states that show P50/P95 and batch size. Also include a tiny calculator widget linked from the landing page.

zoe: Webinar plan: start with one-slide problem statement, show tokens-per-dollar curve, demo a 60s interactive calculator, then a customer vignette and CTA to book a capacity consult.

mike: For demos, we should prepare two concrete example apps (low-throughput chat, high-throughput embedding search) with callouts showing where they land on the curve. Helps PMs map to their product.

elaine: Action items: ryan -> chart specs + sample numbers; zoe -> routing + micro-form fields; mike -> social copy + two app vignettes; i'll assemble methodology and the one-pager. Deadline EOD Wednesday.

product-bot: reminder: include default batch size and hardware footprint in methodology.

elaine: Nicely noted. If anyone finds a competitor visual that nails the "per-dollar" concept, drop it here. We'll iterate on copy tests after the first mock.
